sentences.text: In view of order of this Court dated 11.1.2024 the service of notice on respondent No.1 has been dispensed.
2. Record is received.
Though matter is listed today for orders on admission, however, with consent of learned counsel for the parties, it is finally heard.

3. This appeal under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by appellant/claimant against award dated 29.10.2022 passed by 7th Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Rewa in MACC No.539/2017.

3. The claim petition filed by the appellant before the Tribunal for grant of compensation on account of loss suffered to him due to demolition of shop and house as a result of overturning of a Truck bearing No.MP-19/HA- 7169 has been dismissed on the ground of territorial jurisdiction by observing that accident in question took place in District Sidhi whereas claim petition has been filed in District Rewa.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that Tribunal has not properly appreciated the provision of section 166(2) of Motor Vehicles Act and settled legal position of law that claim cannot be rejected on the ground of jurisdiction if there is branch office of the Insurance Company where claim petition is filed.
It is also submitted respondent/Insurance Company has Office at Rewa as well as Sidhi.
5. Learned counsel for the respondent no.3/Insurance Company has not disputed the Insurance Company has office at Rewa as well as Sidhi, therefore, claim could have been filed at either place.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Tribunal as also the impugned award.
7.
In the case of Malati Sardar Vs.
National
Insurance
Company
Limited and others
3 SCC 43
the Hon'ble Supreme Court in paragraph 14 has held that provision in question is a benevolent provision for the victims of accidents of negligent driving.
The provision for territorial jurisdiction has to be interpreted consistent with objection of facilitating remedies for the victims of accidents.
Hyper technical approach in such mattes can hardly be appreciated.
There is no bar to a claim petition being filed at a place where the Insurance Company, which is main contesting parties in such cases, has its business.
8. Thus, the Tribunal has taken a very hyper technical approach.
The Tribunal has dismissed the claim petition not on merit, but on the ground territorial jurisdiction.
The impugned order dated 29.10.2022 is set aside.

The case is remanded to the Tribunal at Rewa with a direction to afford opportunity to both the parties for presenting their case and thereafter decide the same on merits in accordance with law by ignoring the objection of territorial jurisdiction.
